description: Binning contract shared by the Python atlas pipeline and the web explorer. Change binning only by creating a new version.

D_msh.definition: geometric depth (|r_norm| - R_mp,ref(theta)) / (R_bs,ref(theta) - R_mp,ref(theta)) of the frame's normalized position between the reference boundaries; values inside the clip band but outside the edges go to the first/last bin, others are dropped. In GSM it equals clip(R_norm, 0, 1).

theta_deg.definition: arccos(X/|r|) of the frame's normalized position (X/Y/Z_gsm_norm in GSM, X/Y/Z_pgsm_norm in PGSM); 0 = subsolar

phi_deg.definition: atan2(Z, Y) of the frame's normalized position (PGSM at pgsm.atlas_clock_deg), wrapped to [0, 360); 90 = +Z

frames.GSM: MANGO GSM: space_mango get_data(frame='gsm'); positions X/Y/Z_gsm_norm.
frames.PGSM: MANGO PGSM (Michotte de Welle 2024, thesis 2.7.3-2.7.4): space_mango get_data(frame='pgsm', cone=[0, 180], clock=pgsm.atlas_clock_deg); positions X/Y/Z_pgsm_norm. Every sample appears twice (bx_sign = +1 and -1).

pgsm.rotation: PGSM at a target clock t is R(t - atlas_clock_deg) applied to the atlas, R(a): (Y, Z) -> (Y cos a + Z sin a, -Y sin a + Z cos a): the azimuth atan2(Z, Y) becomes phi - a. Exact for positions, B and V (space_mango, checked to 1e-13).

clock_deg.definition: atan2(By_imf, Bz_imf) wrapped to [0, 360); 0 = northward IMF, 90 = +By

cone_deg.definition: GSM: arccos(Bx_imf / |B_imf|), 0 = IMF sunward. PGSM: space_mango cone_pgsm, the SWI cone measured from -V_sw (f for bx_sign = +1, 180 - f for bx_sign = -1).

V_sw.definition: |V_sw|: from Vx_sw, Vy_sw, Vz_sw in GSM; space_mango's |V_sw| column in PGSM

histogram.quantile_method: cumulative counts, linear interpolation inside the bin in the axis scale (log10 for log axes)

neff.definition: number of distinct (spacecraft, hour) intervals; an optional overlay that hatches cells dominated by few spacecraft passes

row_filter: rows space_mango returns for the frame (paired with OMNI and normalized), with a finite normalized position and finite conditioning angles (cone; clock in GSM)

knn.definition: k is counted in neighbours of the full dataset (default 7000, as in the MANGO statistical studies). Tools holding a random fraction f of the samples search round(k*f) neighbours, which covers the same neighbourhood. Neighbours are the nearest samples (Euclidean, R_E) among the frame's normalized positions; NaN when the distance of the ceil(k/2)-th nearest exceeds cap_re. Only neighbours within search_factor*cap_re are searched. Quantiles use linear interpolation of the neighbours' values in axis space. The sample table keeps a deterministic random fraction (sample_fraction) of the samples; time plays no role.

reference_boundaries.definition: MANGO normalizes magnetosheath positions radially between these mean surfaces: |r_gsm_norm| = R_mp(theta) + clip(R_norm, 0, 1) (R_bs(theta) - R_mp(theta)), theta from X_GSM (checked on 100 % of the MANGO docs sample, max error 1.3e-6 R_E). Source: B. Michotte de Welle, space_bayane/models/planetary.py (mp_shue1998, bs_jelinek2012) at these default parameters.

voxels.definition: Per (frame, condition bin, voxel) the number of samples and the sum of the raw value of each quantity (finite values only). Voxels are cubes of size_re in the normalized frame coordinates; id = (i<<20)|(j<<10)|k with i = floor(x/size_re)+index_offset (same for j with y, k with z).
voxels.knn: For a node, voxels are ordered by the distance d from the node to their centre (ties by id); their counts are accumulated until k samples are reached (the last voxel contributes only the samples still needed). NaN when fewer than ceil(k/2) samples lie within search_factor*cap_re, or when the voxel where the cumulative count reaches ceil(k/2) is farther than cap_re. Value = sum_v w_v * f_v * S_v / sum_v w_v * f_v * N_v with f_v the used fraction of voxel v, S_v and N_v its sum and count, and w_v = 1/max(d_v, size_re/2) for the distance-weighted mean (sklearn KNeighborsRegressor weights='distance') or 1 for the plain mean.

vectors.mapping: Each sample's vector is pushed forward through MANGO's radial normalization r_n = R*_mp + D (R*_bs - R*_mp), D = (r - R_mp)/(R_bs - R_mp): v_r,n = (dR*/dR) v_r + [R*_mp' + D dR*' - dR* (R_mp' + D dR')/dR] v_theta / r, v_theta,n = (r_n/r) v_theta, v_phi,n = (r_n/r) v_phi, with ' = d/dtheta, dR = R_bs - R_mp, * = reference_boundaries. The sample's slopes are the reference slopes scaled by R_mp/R*_mp and R_bs/R*_bs (approximation A1).
vectors.frame: GSM: the served vectors. PGSM: space_mango's B*_pgsm and V*_pgsm with the same pushforward evaluated at the PGSM position (approximation A2: treats the SWI rotation as a rotation about X_GSM; off by the aberration angle, median 5.4 deg).
vectors.voxels: Voxel quantities <name>_x, <name>_y, <name>_z: per (frame, condition bin, voxel) the count of samples with all three mapped components finite and the sum of each component in the frame. The vector field is the voxel k-NN mean of each component (voxels.knn, distance-weighted).
